newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 12.

text.p: -- REUTERS WILL RETURN 613 MILLION STG TO INVESTORS

Information group Reuters has announced that it intends to return some 613 million stg to investors. The company will create a special dividend share to accomplish the payment in a move aimed at reducing its cashpile. The special share will also meet tax regulations in both the U.S. and the U.K. and will be quoted in London and on the U.S. Nasdaq. A previous share buyback scheme had raised taxation concerns at the Treasury.
-- BOOST FOR CLARKE AS JOBLESS TOTAL HITS 5 1/2-YEAR LOW

In what is seen as a boost to the government's hopes for the next general election, figures published on Wednesday reveal that U.K. unemployment has fallen to its lowest level for five-and-a-half years. Additional goods news came with the revelation that, despite the fall, the level of wage inflation in some elements of the jobs market has also fallen. The promising wage inflation figures have also added to speculation that Chancellor Kenneth Clarke may yet opt for another reduction in taxes.
-- TREASURY PLANS TO CURB TAX RELIEF FOR PROFIT-RELATED PAY

It is reported that the Treasury is planning over the next year to reduce the level of tax relief provided to profit-related pay schemes. At present some 2.5 million workers in the U.K. are currently receiving boosts to their take-home pay from such initiatives. However, the cost to the Treasury has risen sharply prompting concern that unless action is taken a major tax revenue shortfall could develop.
-- DEUTSCHE SET TO MAKE THIRD BAILOUT OF MORGAN FUNDS

Deutsche Bank is reported to be preparing for a third time to provide financial support for investment funds managed by its Morgan Grenfell subsidiary. The move comes some two weeks after it was discovered that there had been regulatory breaches in the running of three funds, prompting the suspension of a senior manager. The bank is stepping in once more because of the large numbers of investors involved who have redeemed their funds.
-- FOREIGN BANKS PROTEST OVER LONDON RED TAPE

Members of the Foreign Banks and Securities Houses Association have expressed concern about the level of bureaucracy involved in operating in London. The banks are particularly troubled by the costs involved in form-filling to meet the requirement of maintaining operations in the capital. Members of the association feel that some trade department rules covering non-European Union banks operating in the UK are discriminatory.
-- HANSON ARM SETS UP WORKS COUNCIL DESPITE UK OPT-OUT

Hanson Brick, a subsidiary of the conglomerate Hanson, has become the latest company to establish a works council, effectively ignoring the government's current opt-out from the social chapter of the Maastricht treaty. However, company chairman Lord Hanson has also voiced his opposition to EU legislation in the social field, warning of its adverse impact on competition and productivity.
-- BRUSSELS SETS PHONE SERVICE STANDARDS

The European Commission has announced a series of standards it expects to apply to the provision of telecommunications services across the EU when the sector is liberalised in 1998. A series of basic standards are being set which include the provision of directory inquiry services and public payphones. Those operators who do not meet these standards will be obliged to contribute to a "universal service fund".
-- ITALY TOLD TO GET READY FOR EMU

The Italian federation representing local industrialists has called on the government to make greater efforts to prepare the country for participation in the single European currency. Members of the Confindustria are particularly keen to see action taken to address the country's budget deficit, which they believe may require the application of an extra mini-budget next year. Existing proposals for reductions in public spending have, however, already drawn criticism from the left.
-- SHIPPING LOAN "PUSHED BCCI TO ITS COLLAPSE'

A fraud trial at the Old Bailey has heard how the funding of a shipping empire run by Abbas Gokal played a major role in the eventual collapse of the Bank of Credit and Commerce International. Several hundred million pounds worth of fraudulent loans were made to the business as a result of a conspiracy involving senior officials at the bank, according to a case being brought by Britain's Serious Fraud Office against Gokal.
-- SEA EMPRESS OIL SPILL COST 25 MILLION POUNDS AND 960 JOBS

A report published on Wednesday has estimated that the major oil spill off the coast of Pembrokeshire involving the Sea Empress tanker cost the local economy some 25 million stg and 960 jobs. The tanker grounded in February of this year, spilling 70,000 tonnes of oil, impacting severely on local tourism and the fishing industry. The report also notes that the economy has been further damaged by the BSE crisis and is now on a par with Portuguese levels.
